name: House mouse, male, C57BL/6J
status: Draft for review. Projection strengths and most receptor levels are seeded from the Allen mouse atlases; every sign, and the oxytocin and vasopressin levels, are still a first guess.

regions.name: Main olfactory epithelium
regions.note: Volatile odours carried on the air, so detected at a distance: food, water, the smell of a mark or of another animal.

regions.name: Vomeronasal organ
regions.note: Involatile cues, taken up only when the nose is on the source. This is where the MUP barcode of a urine mark is read.

regions.name: Whiskers
regions.note: Walls, doorways, the body of another animal.

regions.name: Nociceptors
regions.note: A bite, and where on the body it landed.

regions.name: Viscera and blood
regions.note: Energy stores, hydration, bladder fill.

regions.name: Mouth
regions.note: Food or water at the mouth.

regions.name: Retina
regions.note: Light level, day and night.

regions.name: Muscle and balance
regions.note: Own speed and turning, tiredness.

regions.name: Accessory olfactory bulb
regions.note: First brain stage for the MUP barcode.

regions.name: Piriform cortex
regions.note: Learned odour objects. Lateral entorhinal cortex is folded in.

regions.name: Barrel cortex
regions.note: Whisker touch. The thalamic relay is folded in.

regions.name: Parabrachial nucleus
regions.note: Pain, taste and gut signals. The nucleus of the solitary tract is folded in.

regions.name: Arcuate nucleus
regions.note: Hunger (AgRP) and satiety (POMC) cells.

regions.name: Subfornical organ
regions.note: Thirst. Median preoptic nucleus is folded in.

regions.name: Suprachiasmatic nucleus
regions.note: The clock.

regions.name: Medial amygdala
regions.note: Sex and identity of another animal from its odour.

regions.name: Bed nucleus of the stria terminalis
Basolateral amygdala
regions.note: Learned value of cues.

regions.name: Dorsal hippocampus
regions.note: Place. Medial entorhinal cortex is folded in.

regions.name: Hippocampal CA2 and ventral CA1
regions.note: Memory for individuals.

regions.name: Paraventricular hypothalamus
regions.note: Source of oxytocin, vasopressin and the stress response.

regions.name: Lateral hypothalamus
regions.note: Feeding, drinking, arousal.

regions.name: Medial prefrontal cortex
regions.note: Rank and effort in contests. Anterior cingulate and secondary motor cortex are folded in.

regions.name: Mediodorsal thalamus
regions.note: Its input to prefrontal cortex strengthens with a history of winning.

regions.name: Medial preoptic area
regions.note: Mating, parental care, scent marking.

regions.name: Ventromedial hypothalamus, ventrolateral part
regions.note: Attack.

regions.name: Ventral premammillary nucleus
regions.note: Male odour to aggression.

regions.name: Lateral septum
regions.note: Brakes attack; fed by the hippocampus.

regions.name: Central amygdala
regions.note: Defensive output.

regions.name: Ventral tegmental area
regions.note: Source of dopamine.

regions.name: Lateral habenula
regions.note: Outcomes worse than expected, defeat.

regions.name: Dorsal raphe
regions.note: Source of serotonin.

regions.name: Periaqueductal grey
regions.note: Bite, flight, freezing.

regions.name: Superior colliculus
regions.note: Orienting and turning.

regions.name: Mesencephalic locomotor region
regions.note: Speed.

regions.name: Barrington's nucleus
regions.note: Two cell types: one contracts the bladder wall, one relaxes the urethral sphincter.

regions.name: Neck and trunk
regions.note: Turning: the left unit minus the right unit. In the engine today.

regions.name: Limbs
regions.note: Speed. In the engine today.

regions.name: Jaw
regions.note: Biting. In the engine with contest physics on.

regions.name: Bladder wall
regions.note: Contracts to push urine out.

regions.name: Urethral sphincter
regions.note: Held shut by default. Urine leaves when it relaxes while the bladder wall contracts; the mark is what that leaves on the ground.

modulators.name: Oxytocin
modulators.basis: Levels as drafted. The receptor genes are too weakly expressed in the Allen in situ data to tell absent from undetected.

modulators.name: Vasopressin
modulators.source_note: Paraventricular hypothalamus, plus steroid-dependent cells in BNST and medial amygdala that are denser in males.
modulators.basis: Levels as drafted. The receptor genes are too weakly expressed in the Allen in situ data to tell absent from undetected.

modulators.name: Dopamine
modulators.basis: Levels from Allen in situ expression of Drd1, Drd2 (adult male C57BL/6J). A level the atlas does not see is kept at 1: in situ signal shows where a receptor is made, not where it sits on incoming terminals.

modulators.name: Serotonin
modulators.basis: Levels from Allen in situ expression of Htr1a, Htr1b, Htr2a, Htr2c (adult male C57BL/6J). A level the atlas does not see is kept at 1: in situ signal shows where a receptor is made, not where it sits on incoming terminals.

modulators.name: Opioids
modulators.source_note: Beta-endorphin from arcuate POMC cells; enkephalin and dynorphin are released locally.
modulators.basis: Levels from Allen in situ expression of Oprd1, Oprk1, Oprm1 (adult male C57BL/6J). A level the atlas does not see is kept at 1: in situ signal shows where a receptor is made, not where it sits on incoming terminals.

modulators.name: Stress (CRF)
modulators.source_note: Paraventricular hypothalamus, central amygdala and BNST.
modulators.basis: Levels from Allen in situ expression of Crhr1, Crhr2 (adult male C57BL/6J). A level the atlas does not see is kept at 1: in situ signal shows where a receptor is made, not where it sits on incoming terminals.

modulators.name: Gonadal steroids
modulators.source_note: Testes, outside the brain. Acts through androgen receptors and, after conversion to oestradiol, oestrogen receptors.
modulators.basis: Levels from Allen in situ expression of Ar, Esr1 (adult male C57BL/6J). A level the atlas does not see is kept at 1: in situ signal shows where a receptor is made, not where it sits on incoming terminals.

leroy2018.finding: CA2 output to the lateral septum promotes aggression by disinhibiting the ventrolateral ventromedial hypothalamus; vasopressin strengthens it.

wong2016.finding: The lateral septum's projection to the ventromedial hypothalamus suppresses attack.

zhou2017.finding: Mediodorsal thalamic input to dorsomedial prefrontal cortex carries the lasting effect of a history of winning on rank.

padilla2016.finding: AgRP hunger neurons that project to the medial amygdala, and on to the BNST, suppress territorial aggression in the starved state.

hou2016.finding: Crh neurons of Barrington's nucleus drive bladder contraction and take input from higher areas, including the medial preoptic area; male marking depends on odour and rank.

stagkourakis2018.finding: Ventral premammillary neurons trigger attack through their projection to the ventrolateral ventromedial hypothalamus; a brief manipulation switches dominance for weeks.

han2015.finding: CGRP neurons of the parabrachial nucleus relay pain to the central amygdala.

lin2011.finding: Stimulating the ventrolateral ventromedial hypothalamus makes a male attack; silencing it stops fighting between males.

chamero2007.finding: MUPs activate vomeronasal neurons and promote fighting between males only through the vomeronasal pathway.

evans2018.finding: A weak excitatory connection from the medial superior colliculus to the dorsal periaqueductal grey sets the threshold for escape.

wang2011.finding: Raising or lowering synaptic strength in dorsal medial prefrontal cortex moves a mouse up or down in rank.

hitti2014.finding: Silencing CA2 abolishes memory for another individual and leaves other hippocampal memory intact.

li2018.finding: Inhibitory lateral hypothalamic cells projecting to the periaqueductal grey drive predatory attack; excitatory ones drive evasion.

hong2014.finding: Inhibitory medial amygdala cells promote aggression; neighbouring excitatory cells promote self-grooming.

falkner2020.finding: The ventrolateral ventromedial hypothalamus excites the lateral periaqueductal grey, whose activity is locked to biting.

franklin2017.finding: Social defeat weakens the prefrontal projection to the dorsal periaqueductal grey; inhibiting it mimics the avoidance defeat produces.

idea_mup.finding: Every C57 male carries the same MUP barcode, so his urine marks carry no identity information, with knock-on effects on behaviour.

keller2018.finding: A second cell type in Barrington's nucleus relaxes the urethral sphincter and lets a male urinate at will, as in scent marking.

idea_muscle.finding: The output is muscle, not a mark: urine leaves when the sphincter relaxes and the bladder wall presses, and the mark is the physical result left in the environment.

idea_vno.finding: The vomeronasal organ should fire only when the animal is on a urine mark and investigating it; volatile odour at a distance belongs to the main olfactory epithelium.

allen_conn.finding: A measurable projection in the Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas (Oh et al. 2014, adult C57BL/6J). Its strength here is the atlas tercile among these areas. The atlas does not give a sign.

allen_absent.cite: Not seen in the Allen atlas
allen_absent.finding: No measurable projection between these areas in the Allen connectivity atlas. Kept from the draft at the lowest strength until someone checks it; a few injections missing a pathway is not proof that it is absent.

sign_by_cell_type.finding: Added because the atlas shows it. Its sign is assigned from the main cell type of the source area and needs checking.

left_out: Sensory thalamus, motor cortex, dorsal striatum, cerebellum, locus coeruleus, anterior hypothalamus and the predator-defence nuclei.
